content: This medication is intended for application to the distal rectum in patients who are unable to retain steroid enemas. However, its safety and efficacy for this purpose have not been firmly established. Potential adverse effects include burning, dryness, folliculitis, hypopigmentation, itching, pain, rectal bleeding, and secondary infections. Hypersensitivity reactions have been documented. It is contraindicated in cases of obstruction, abscess, perforation, peritonitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, extensive fistulas, and sinus tracts. Always adhere to the usage instructions provided on the product carton. Sigmoidoscopy is recommended to evaluate the treatment course rather than relying solely on symptomatic improvement. Do not insert any part of the aerosol container directly into the anus, as the contents are under pressure. Avoid burning or puncturing the aerosol container, and do not store it at temperatures exceeding 120°F. Since this product is not expelled, systemic absorption of hydrocortisone may be greater than that from corticosteroid enema formulations. If there is no clinical or proctologic improvement within two to three weeks of initiating therapy, or if the patient’s condition worsens, discontinue the medication. Rarely, anaphylactoid reactions have been reported in patients receiving corticosteroid therapy. In patients with latent tuberculosis or tuberculin reactivity, close monitoring is necessary as reactivation of the disease may occur. During prolonged corticosteroid therapy, such patients should receive chemoprophylaxis. Administration of live or live-attenuated vaccines is contraindicated in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids. Killed or inactivated vaccines may be administered, but the response to these vaccines cannot be predicted. Immunization procedures may be undertaken in patients receiving corticosteroids as replacement therapy, such as for Addison’s disease. The lowest effective dose of corticosteroid should be used to manage the condition under treatment. If dosage reduction is possible, it should be done gradually. Complications from glucocorticoid treatment depend on the dose and duration of therapy. A risk-benefit analysis must be conducted for each individual case to determine the appropriate dose, duration, and whether daily or intermittent therapy should be employed. Kaposi’s sarcoma has been reported in patients undergoing corticosteroid therapy, particularly for chronic conditions. Discontinuation of corticosteroids may lead to clinical improvement. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; corticosteroids should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Infants born to mothers who received corticosteroids during pregnancy should be carefully monitored for signs of hypoadrenalism. Systemically administered corticosteroids can appear in human milk and may suppress growth, interfere with endogenous corticosteroid production, or cause other adverse effects. Caution should be exercised when administering corticosteroids to nursing women. This medication decreases inflammation by suppressing the migration of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) and reversing increased capillary permeability. Its absorption is limited, with an onset of action typically occurring within 5 to 7 days. Hydrocortisone rectal cream or ointment is commonly marketed under brand names such as Anusol-HC, Proctocream-HC, and Proctosol-HC. It is used to treat minor pain, itching, swelling, and discomfort caused by hemorrhoids and other anal area conditions, such as anal fissures and itching. To apply the product inside the anus, use the applicator tip, cap, or nozzle as directed in the product package or by your doctor. Fill the applicator with medication as instructed and insert it approximately 5 centimeters into the anus. Apply the medication in and around the anal opening as directed. Do not use your finger to apply the medication inside the anus. Do not cover the treated area with plastic or waterproof bandages unless instructed by your doctor, as this may increase the absorption of the medication through the skin. Wash your hands immediately after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, ears, or mouth. This product is typically used 2 to 4 times daily, after each bowel movement, or as directed by your doctor. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Use this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. Do not use more of this product, use it more frequently, or continue using it longer than prescribed by your doctor. If you have been using this medication for a long time or in high doses, do not stop using it suddenly without your doctor’s approval, as some conditions may worsen when the drug is abruptly discontinued. Common side effects include redness, burning, or itching at the application site. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, leading to systemic corticosteroid side effects. These effects are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for extended periods. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this product, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to hydrocortisone or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Rarely, prolonged use of corticosteroid medications can impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. Although unlikely, this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth if used for extended periods. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It should not be used for long periods or in large amounts. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as cortisol levels) may be performed while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another condition unless directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not refrigerate. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
